items.title: Antonelli leads extended FP2 amid Friday setbacks
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli set 1:23.077, 0.127 seconds ahead of George Russell; Lando Norris was third at +0.445s. The FIA Document 21 table matches Formula1.com across all 22 classified drivers. Two red flags interrupted FP2, which was extended by 13 minutes; Gasly's high-speed spin brought one. Leclerc said his earlier FP2 spin damaged the Ferrari floor; he and Hamilton finished seventh and eighth in both Friday sessions as Ferrari searched for pace. A Virtual Safety Car followed when Hamilton stopped after reporting lost power; Ferrari said it was investigating and did not consider it a concern for Saturday. Norris estimated McLaren was 0.6–0.7 seconds per lap off, while The Race’s traffic-adjusted analysis put Antonelli’s long-run average 0.810 seconds per lap ahead of Verstappen.
items.why_it_matters: The classification is official. Leclerc described the floor damage; Ferrari said Hamilton's power issue was under investigation, not a confirmed cause. Gasly's explanation is his account: he attributed the bottoming to cooler tyres and lower pressures, not a confirmed mechanical fault. The Norris gap and The Race long-run figure are Friday estimates, not a representative race-pace forecast or qualifying result.

items.title: FIA fines Audi €500 for Hülkenberg pit-lane speeding
items.summary: Document 20 records Car 27 at 84.4 km/h in the 80 km/h pit lane during FP2. The €500 fine is imposed on Audi Revolut F1 Team, not the driver.
items.why_it_matters: This is a team fine, not a grid penalty or sporting penalty for Hülkenberg.

items.title: Localized tyre-wear indicators prompt a Pirelli review
items.summary: The Race reports localized 100% wear indicators on the most-abused front-left tyres after 15 laps of high-fuel running. Pirelli is examining returned tyres and has not announced a pressure increase or shorter stint limit. FIA Document 13 V2 still specifies a 27-lap cap and 29.0 psi minimum front slick starting pressure; Document 25 reports listed checks compliant but publishes no revised table. Formula1.com still conflicts on pre-weekend sets (2/3/8 plus a Q3 Soft versus 2/4/7); neither is a remaining-set inventory.
items.why_it_matters: A localized wear indicator is not evidence that a whole tyre wore through. Treat any pressure or stint-limit change as pending until Pirelli or the FIA confirms it, and keep the allocation discrepancy attributed.

sources.label: Pirelli official Qatar tyre briefing, 24 November

items.title: Verstappen says Red Bull is still searching for balance
items.summary: Verstappen finished fifth in FP2 after a day when he and Hadjar struggled with understeer. Verstappen described the balance as disconnected; technical director Pierre Wache said the fixes moved the car in the right direction but he was unsure how much of Mercedes' gap Red Bull could close.
items.why_it_matters: This is a Friday assessment rather than a prediction of qualifying or race pace.

sources.label: Formula1.com Friday Red Bull balance report

items.title: Alonso returns after missing Qatar FP1
items.summary: Formula1.com reports that Fernando Alonso returned in FP2 after missing Thursday media day while recovering from a virus. Jak Crawford drove Alonso's Aston Martin in FP1.
items.why_it_matters: Crawford's FP1 appearance was a practice substitution, not a change to the race line-up.
